issues.description: Cleanup moved into defer means a panic mid-iteration leaves no state — fine, but the old eager reset on entry is gone, so a caller that reuses the Sorter after a panic is now relying entirely on defer ordering.
issues.detail: Previously state was cleared on entry. Now cleanup is only in the deferred function. If yield panics, defer runs and that's fine. But the explicit `s.stack = s.stack[0:]` on entry is gone too. Belt-and-suspenders would keep an entry-time reset as a guard. Not a blocker; document the invariant.

issues.description: Behavior change: `s.state[k] = sorted` now only fires when `state != sorted`, dropping the unconditional write.
issues.detail: Old code always set sorted after pop. New code only sets it inside the `state != sorted` branch. For nodes already marked sorted being re-popped, the write is redundant anyway — so this is likely equivalent, but the commit message says nothing about it. Either justify in the message or revert to unconditional. Reviewer shouldn't have to prove equivalence.

issues.description: Typos in the comment: "visisted" and "if its".
issues.detail: If you're rewriting the comment, spell the words right. "visisted" should be "visited" and "if its" should be "if it's". The comment is the part future-you reads; don't ship it sloppy.

issues.description: Collapsing `working` and `walking` into one state is good taste — eliminates a special case — but the commit message doesn't say why the old two-state machine existed.
issues.detail: Removing `working` is the GOOD-TASTE move: one fewer state, same semantics. But the original author presumably distinguished them for a reason (or thought they did). The message says "reduces the internal states" without explaining why the distinction was spurious. One sentence on why the merge is safe would save the next maintainer ten minutes.

issues.description: THREE-PATCHES: state reduction, stack cleanup fix, and yield-ordering change are three logical fixes in one diff.
issues.detail: The PR description literally lists three things: "reduces the internal states, fixes non-zero elements in the stack slice and fixes cleanup by clearing state on completion." That's three patches. Each should be bisectable on its own. For a 30-line diff I won't die on this hill, but the discipline matters.

issues.description: No test added or referenced for the stack-reuse bug being fixed.
issues.detail: The PR claims it fixes "non-zero elements in the stack slice" — meaning the prior code had a real bug where reusing a Sorter left garbage. Where's the regression test? A bug fix without a test that fails before and passes after is a bug fix on the honor system. Add a test that calls Sort twice on the same Sorter and proves the second run is clean.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The core change is good taste — collapsing `working`/`walking` into one state eliminates a special case, and moving cleanup into the defer is correct. But this is three patches masquerading as one, the commit message doesn't justify the semantic changes, the comment rewrite has typos, and there's no regression test for the stack-reuse bug it claims to fix. Land it after splitting, fixing the comment, and adding a test that exercises Sorter reuse.
